catalog_quote: Suprasegmentals (tone, stress, length) Stress genarally falls on the first syllable of multisyllable words. The main exception is in verbs with tense and aspectual prefixes. In this case stress falls on the first syllable of the verb stem or root.

audit.recode_to: Drop 'fixed(-unreviewed) initial'. Recode as contested/partly lexical: disyllables carry lexically contrastive stress (penult vs final, minimal pairs; Blust 2021 pp. 169-170), trisyllables regularly initial (150+ items), 4+-syllable words initial secondary with primary on the final or penult; final-stressed disyllabic stems retract to initial phrase-internally. Keep Martin OPD 1999 / CAD 1995 'generally initial, stem-initial after TAM prefixes' as the dissenting source in 'contra', with the fieldwork-depth caveat (Blust: 5 days, two teenage speakers, 1975; Martin: resident fieldworker, 2-sentence statement). If the catalog must keep a single class, 'lexical/unpredictable (disyllables) with initial default' is closer to the fuller source than 'fixed initial'.
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: the deciding quotation is verbatim on p. 3 of the held OPD PDF under 'Suprasegmentals (tone, stress, length)', and the same claim is independently present in the held Martin 1995 CAD introduction p. 669 sec. 2.3.
